summary.framework_interpretation: BLINDED-FORWARD-TEST NOTE: The cohort metadata names F-35 avionics, T-7 cockpit, Sentinel ICBM ground subsystems, NNSA nuclear modernization, T55/F124/ATK-3000 engines as HON's defense programs. The 10-K itself NEVER names any of these programs — disclosure is aggregated to 'Defense and Space business unit' ($7.22B FY25) and 'DoD direct sales' ($4.21B FY25). This is the opposite of the J-BOOK EXPOSURE DIVERGENCE PATTERN this cohort tests for: HON does NOT make program-element-specific forward-revenue claims, so there is no narrow falsifiable PE-level claim to catch in divergence. Where J-Book corpus does contain cohort-implied programs (F-35 C2D2: FUNDED_STEADY; Minuteman/Sentinel PE 0101213F: FUNDED_GROWING), the trajectories are healthy. Where corpus lacks coverage (Sentinel GBSD, T-7, NNSA, T55, F124), severity defaults to UNVERIFIABLE per heuristic 7. usaspending confirms $6.41B of historical Honeywell DoD obligated activity (including T55 engine procurement explicitly), so the past-revenue base is real. Net result: PASS-dominant scoring; the framework correctly does NOT manufacture a divergence signal when the filing makes only macro-level claims and the M-sources show no contradictions.
